findings.observed: `aws_sqs_queue.work["orders"]` will be destroyed because its for_each key changed, and `aws_sqs_queue.work["order_events"]` will be created with the same `name` ("fixture-lifecycle-orders"). A shared identity suggests a possible address rename; it does not establish that these are the same cloud object. The SQS queue would be destroyed with it, losing every message still in the queue.
findings.recommendation: Confirm that both entries refer to the same provider configuration, account, region and cloud object before considering a moved block (`from = aws_sqs_queue.work["orders"]`, `to = aws_sqs_queue.work["order_events"]`). Otherwise review the intended migration and any uniqueness constraints on name.
findings.title: `aws_sqs_queue.work["orders"]` and `aws_sqs_queue.work["order_events"]` share an identity across a destroy/create pair: possible address rename

findings.observed: The IAM role is replaced because `name` ("fixture-lifecycle-deploy-v1" → "fixture-lifecycle-deploy-v2") cannot be changed in place. The new object is created before the old one is destroyed (create_before_destroy).
findings.recommendation: Check that the identifiers other systems hold for this resource (ARN, ID, DNS name, IP) are not referenced outside Terraform, or plan a cutover.
findings.title: `aws_iam_role.deploy` will be destroyed and recreated

findings.observed: The SQS queue's `policy` comes from a value the plan cannot show (a data source, a template or an attribute of another resource).
findings.recommendation: Review the policy document in the pull request, or build it with `data.aws_iam_policy_document` in the same configuration so the plan carries it.
findings.title: `aws_sqs_queue.work["order_events"]`: `policy` is not known until apply, so it was not assessed
